sentences.text: "This is the fight of our lives," he repeatedly told his party.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: The focus, much like his conference speech last year, was on Reform UK.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: But the announcement he'd held back for his speech was aimed at Conservative-leaning voters: tax cuts worth billions.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: And not just for lower income earners, but for those in the higher 40% rate of tax too.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: Part of the announcement – raising the amount you can earn before you pay income tax altogether – was the same policy Davey's bête noire, Reform UK, announced at their conference a couple of weeks ago.

sentences.text: The dividing line he drew was over how it was paid for.

sentences.text: But the plan is speculative.

sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: Plenty of economic experts, including the official budget forecaster the OBR, believe the UK's economy could grow if the UK was in the Single Market.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: But as recent political history teaches us, negotiating a deal with the European Union is often more difficult than party leaders hope.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: And basing a tax cut on potential future economic growth is a risky business.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: There is also uncertainty over whether the Lib Dems' sums add up.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: The independent  think tank, the Institute for Fiscal Studies, said the policy as set out in the press release would cost "much more" than the £17bn the Lib Dems have budgeted for.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: The party says the tax cut wouldn't come in until the fifth year after the next election.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: But the Lib Dem MPs I spoke to afterwards were less focused on these details than the message it sent to voters.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: Davey came into this conference facing criticism over his leadership from some MPs in private and others in his party in public worrying about the party's ambition and direction.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: For now those concerns have been dampened.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: One told me they would rather the focus had been wooing younger voters by tackling the amount graduates repay in student loans, an old bruise for the Lib Dems.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: But overall this speech, and this conference, was well received by the Lib Dem faithful.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: They are a party honing their messaging before the next general election.

sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.article_title: Lib Dems leave conference buoyed by Davey's message

sentences.text: El Niño is a naturally-occurring pattern, which happens about every two to seven years and tends to last for around a year.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Trade winds that typically blow from east to west across the Pacific Ocean can weaken or even reverse, allowing warm water to spread eastwards.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Heat is then released from the ocean into the atmosphere which can boost global temperatures and drive changes in weather patterns around the world.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Forecasters track the development of El Niño by watching temperatures in a key region of the Pacific Ocean.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: When these are consistently 0.5C above normal, an El Niño is declared.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: There are different ways of measuring the strength of El Niño, however.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: The records that have now been broken relate to daily measurements of sea surface temperature compared with the long term historical average.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: This is called the Oceanic Niño Index (ONI).
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Many scientists - including forecasters in the USA and Australia - also consider an alternative measure known as the Relative Oceanic Niño Index (RONI).
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: This measures how warm the key El Niño region is relative to the rest of the tropical oceans, meaning it takes into account the background warming caused by climate change.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: By the RONI index the current El Niño is not yet a record-breaker - but it is likely that more announcements will follow in the coming weeks.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Professor Adam Scaife, Head of Long Range Prediction at the Met Office, said: "We have been signalling for months that the developing El Niño will be an unprecedented event.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: "The fact that it has already exceeded previous records – with several weeks to go before it peaks later this year – shows the enormity of this El Niño." Every El Niño is different, therefore impacts on global weather patterns are not guaranteed.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: And the unprecedented strength of this El Niño does not necessarily mean it will have unprecedented impacts on the weather.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Professor Scaife said: "Scientists are still assessing whether the impacts will be in proportion to its magnitude, but we are already seeing expected effects worldwide." El Niño increases the odds of storms and floods in some regions and of drought and wildfires in others.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: This video can not be played Watch: How does El Niño affect world weather?
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: El Niño years tend to bring below-average monsoon rainfall in India, which is already being reflected in this year's data.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Statistics from the India Meteorological Department show that, until 22 September the southwest monsoon had brought 15% less rain than normal.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Another typical impact of El Niño is reduced hurricane activity in the Atlantic due to changes in wind patterns high in the atmosphere.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: So far in 2026 there have been no Atlantic hurricanes, setting a new record for the latest date without a hurricane forming since satellite monitoring of storms began.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: Other possible effects - some of which are already being felt - include the increased risk of floods in coastal parts of Ecuador, Peru and the southern USA, and the enhanced threat of drought and wildfires in Brazil, Australia and Indonesia.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: These weather impacts can have significant knock on effects for on crop yields, food security and economies around the globe.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: The UK is thousands of miles from the tropical Pacific and so the effects of El Niño tend to be less clear-cut than in other regions.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: However, it does bring the increased chance of wet and stormy conditions across north-west Europe during the late autumn and early winter.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: A forecast released by the Met Office this autumn stated that there were already "signals for increased rainfall and storminess in autumn here in the UK", especially into November and December.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: The winter of 2015 and 2016, which coincided with a very strong El Niño, brought a succession of major storms delivering what experts at the time described as the most extreme flooding on record.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: In addition to storminess, El Niño can also be associated with UK cold spells in the late winter - but the link is not a strong one and the past evidence is mixed.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: The so-called Big Freeze of winter 2009/2010 was, at the time, the coldest in three decades - and this coincided with an El Niño.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: However, 2006/2007 was also an El Niño winter and that was unseasonably warm.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: As this unprecedented El Niño approaches its likely peak towards the end of 2026, scientists will continue to monitor its development - and its impact on weather around the world.
sentences.article_title: Developing El Niño becomes strongest on record weeks before expected peak

sentences.text: An unexpected surge in government borrowing in August, driven by persistently higher inflation, has added to pressure on Chancellor John Healey as he prepares to deliver his first Budget at the end of October.
sentences.article_title: Unexpected UK borrowing surge adds to pre-Budget pressure on chancellor

sentences.text: Borrowing - the difference between tax receipts and government spending - was £18.3bn in August, almost a fifth higher than the year before, the Office for National Statistics (ONS) said.
sentences.article_title: Unexpected UK borrowing surge adds to pre-Budget pressure on chancellor

sentences.text: That figure was £3.5bn more than official forecasters expected.
sentences.article_title: Unexpected UK borrowing surge adds to pre-Budget pressure on chancellor

sentences.text: Inflation rose to its highest rate in five months in August in the UK, driven up by higher petrol and diesel prices.
sentences.article_title: Unexpected UK borrowing surge adds to pre-Budget pressure on chancellor

sentences.text: Although tax receipts were higher in August compared with a year ago, spending on public services, benefits, and other costs grew more as the pace of price rises increased.
sentences.article_title: Unexpected UK borrowing surge adds to pre-Budget pressure on chancellor

sentences.text: The interest the government is paying on its debt rose to £8.8bn, its highest August level since records began in 1997.
sentences.article_title: Unexpected UK borrowing surge adds to pre-Budget pressure on chancellor

sentences.text: The cost of servicing that debt comes as the government is under pressure to spend more on defence and cost-of-living support to households, said Martin Beck, chief economist at WPI Strategy.
sentences.article_title: Unexpected UK borrowing surge adds to pre-Budget pressure on chancellor

sentences.text: He said it was important not to "overinterpret a single month given the volatility in the numbers", but added that there were some "concerning elements".
sentences.article_title: Unexpected UK borrowing surge adds to pre-Budget pressure on chancellor

sentences.article_title: Unexpected UK borrowing surge adds to pre-Budget pressure on chancellor

sentences.text: "But even there, the chancellor's got problems," he said.
sentences.article_title: Unexpected UK borrowing surge adds to pre-Budget pressure on chancellor

sentences.text: "The cost of that interest has gone up.

sentences.article_title: Unexpected UK borrowing surge adds to pre-Budget pressure on chancellor

sentences.article_title: Unexpected UK borrowing surge adds to pre-Budget pressure on chancellor

sentences.article_title: Unexpected UK borrowing surge adds to pre-Budget pressure on chancellor

sentences.article_title: Unexpected UK borrowing surge adds to pre-Budget pressure on chancellor

sentences.text: Scientists say they have discovered why the bacteria responsible for the UK's worst outbreak of meningitis B in Kent earlier this year proved so dangerous.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: More than 20 young people, mostly students, were infected in the March outbreak , linked to a Canterbury nightclub.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: All needed hospital treatment, while nine ended up in intensive care and two died.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Experts at the UK Health Security Agency (UKHSA) and the University of Oxford, who have looked at the DNA of the bacterium , external , say it picked up some genetic material from other bugs found naturally in the throats of some people.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: This exchange created a new strain or variant that then spread between clubbers and caused severe illness.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Experts stress the meningitis vaccine currently being offered to more than a million young people starting university protects against it.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Young people can book to get their Men B vaccine at high street pharmacies across England.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: There are walk-in appointments too , external .
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Dr Charlene Rodrigues, consultant in Pathogen Genomics at UKHSA, said: "This investigation shows just how quickly and dramatically these bacteria can change.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: "The fact this outbreak variant was able to spread to so many young people was due to the social environment, a place where lots of close social mixing takes place." Speaking exclusively to the BBC, she said bacteria are known to undergo changes like this, known as horizontal gene transfer.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Such changes can make infections more severe, and may mean they get past the immune system because people haven't encountered them before.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: These events, while rare and unpredictable, could happen again, so experts "should not take their eye off the ball", she added.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Scientists say speed and severity of the Kent outbreak was very unusual .
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: It was described as "unprecedented" and "explosive" at the time, with so many infections happening in one place and over a very short period.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Two people died - a 21-year-old University of Kent student and Juliette Kenny, a sixth-form pupil at Queen Elizabeth's Grammar School in Faversham.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: The outbreak is thought to have started in a nightclub called Club Chemistry in the city centre, which was popular with university students.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: It's likely one person brought the infection in with them, and then it spread that evening.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Meningitis is passed through close contact - including kissing and sharing drinks or vapes.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Dr Rodrigues suspects the very same genetic changes that made the strain so dangerous may also explain why the outbreak was short-lived and did not continue to spread.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: People were generally too sick to be silent carriers who can pass it on unknowingly to others.
sentences.article_title: Scientists discover why Kent meningitis outbreak was so severe

sentences.text: Prof Robert Heyderman, an expert in infectious diseases at University College London, said the outbreak strain could have been carried by healthy people for some time before the conditions were right for the outbreak to occur.

sentences.text: Written prescription fees from vets will be capped at £21 as part of a raft of changes that practices will be legally required to bring in over the coming months.
sentences.article_title: Vet prescription fees capped under rule changes

sentences.text: Vets must also tell clients if cheaper medicine is available online, write price estimates ahead of treatment, and publish price lists for services as part of the rule updates.
sentences.article_title: Vet prescription fees capped under rule changes

sentences.text: The official competition watchdog has brought the measures into force after its investigation into the sector found prices had been rising at nearly twice the rate of inflation.
sentences.article_title: Vet prescription fees capped under rule changes

sentences.text: However, critics say the measures will hit independent vets hardest and will benefit the six firms that own more than two-thirds of practices.
sentences.article_title: Vet prescription fees capped under rule changes

sentences.text: The Competition and Markets Authority (CMA) made its remedies for the sector legally binding as of Tuesday and vets have up to 12 months to bring all the changes in.
sentences.article_title: Vet prescription fees capped under rule changes

sentences.text: The timelines for when vets need to bring in the fixes depends on the exact regulation and the group's size.
sentences.article_title: Vet prescription fees capped under rule changes

sentences.text: The CMA sets it out here. , external "The changes that are being required are changes that will help inform pet owners about prices," said CMA panel chair Martin Coleman.
sentences.article_title: Vet prescription fees capped under rule changes

sentences.text: Cate Titterton believes vets will have to put up prices for things like consultations and surgeries However, Cate Titterton, the owner of an independent vet service in Saltburn, told the BBC the changes will make trips to the vets more expensive for customers.
sentences.article_title: Vet prescription fees capped under rule changes

sentences.text: Families affected by the maternity scandal said the incident was "extremely unnerving" A trust at the centre of the largest maternity scandal in NHS history has revealed it lost historical data during routine IT work, with police now assessing its impact.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: Maternity records of women and babies who received care between September 2011 and November 2022 were overwritten during work at Nottingham University Hospitals (NUH) NHS Trust.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: Information has been restored since the "human error" on 18 August, but the trust has not been able to restore the history showing who viewed maternity records during this period.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: A police probe last year into a missing data file containing the details of hundreds of maternity cases found it was most likely deleted "intentionally or maliciously" .
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: Nottinghamshire Police has been notified of the data incident and is assessing whether there has been any impact on Operation Perth - the investigation into deaths and injuries related to maternity care at Nottingham City Hospital and Queen's Medical Centre, the main two hospitals run by the trust.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: The force said it was told of the data loss on 4 September, and added officers attended NUH on 7 September to establish what happened and how, to consider any potential criminal offences and to find out if the lost data could be recovered.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: Deputy Chief Constable Rob Griffin, gold commander for Operation Perth, said: "At present, no crime has been identified.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: We have received a report from the individual concerned and have spoken with them.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: "Further assessment is ongoing, and we are awaiting analysis of the digital process that was used.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: "In relation to recovery, we are awaiting a copy of the database, before any further attempts can be made.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: We anticipate receiving this during the course of the week.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: "The overall impact on Operation Perth remains under assessment and we will be in a better position to provide a fuller update once the outstanding analysis and recovery work has been completed.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: Officials at NUH said the latest error occurred while a copy of a radiotherapy database was being created.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: A setting that should have been changed, before a set of pre-written computer instructions was run, was "missed" and the process was carried out on a maternity database instead, causing records to be overwritten.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: The trust has restored clinical information, including notes, observations and test results, but has been unable to restore a complete history of who viewed records.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: It means "in most cases", the trust may be unable to confirm whether a maternity record was viewed by a particular person between September 2011 and November 2022.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: Information about current maternity patients has not been affected and no patient information was "accessed or used inappropriately" after the incident, NUH added.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: The trust said the Information Commissioner's Office (ICO) was notified and that it had taken steps to improve its technical processes to prevent a similar incident.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: Andy Callow, chief digital and information officer at NUH, said: "I am sorry for the concern and distress this incident may cause to women and families affected.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: "On 18 August 2026, a human error during a routine technical process resulted in a maternity records database being unintentionally overwritten.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: We took immediate action to investigate the incident and recover the affected information." A statement from the Nottingham Maternity Family Group - which represents many of those affected by the wider scandal - said the incident was "extremely unnerving".
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: "Families who have already endured preventable harm, injury and bereavement should not also have to worry about the security of the records of their experiences," it said.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: "The ability to trust NHS professionals to look after both patients and their data is paramount, but far too many Nottingham families feel that the NUH has fallen short of this.
sentences.article_title: NHS trust blames 'human error' for new baby data loss

sentences.text: Deputy leader Daisy Cooper says she has a plan for growth Liberal Democrat deputy leader Daisy Cooper has warned the UK's economic growth is being held back by a "computer says no" approach.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: Speaking on stage in Brighton, she said: "We build brilliant start-ups, and watch too many leave to scale somewhere else.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: "The system holds it back.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: "In power, we will strike the deal on the single market, we will strike the deal on a customs union, we will strike the deal on defence." She claimed the Lib Dems would say "what no other party dares to say" that Britain "belongs at the heart of Europe, and we will take her there".
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems vow to end 'computer says no' economy to boost growth

sentences.text: Farmer Juan Ángel Izquierdo says it is hard not to worry about wildfires In a small green meadow in the Gredos mountains, west of Madrid, a couple of dozen cows belonging to Juan Ángel Izquierdo and his family are grazing.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The only noise is the gentle clang of the bells around the animals' necks.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This would be an idyllic scene were it not for the blackened pine and oak trees all around, the legacy of a devastating recent wildfire.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was immense, I've never seen anything like it," says Izquierdo, whose family have been farming here for 200 years.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The fire, in late July, merged with two others, burning a total of around 80,000 hectares (200,000 acres), making it the biggest blaze Spain has ever registered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: It consumed more than two-thirds of Izquierdo's land and killed 12 of his 85 cows.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another eight animals had to be put down because of their injuries.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: All the hay he had gathered to feed his cows in the winter was also burned.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "For us farmers, the summers are becoming more and more worrying, because they are getting hotter," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It rains less, the wet season ends earlier and the autumn starts much later." For farmers, such conditions are synonymous with fires.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "If you don't think about the wildfires too much, you feel okay," Izquierdo says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "But when a fire starts in a nearby village you start wondering – 'and what if we're next?'." Wildfires are one of several symptoms of climate change which in recent years have had a substantial impact on Spain's economy, as well as contributing to shocking human tragedies.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: World Weather Attribution, an international research organisation, found that the extreme conditions that drove record-breaking fires in Spain and Portugal in 2025 were 40 times more likely , external to happen due to the warming climate.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The ultimate reason for the greater frequency and intensity of these kinds of fires has to be attributed to the increase in greenhouse gases caused mainly by the generalised use of fossil fuels," said Ernesto Rodríguez Camino, president of the Spanish Meteorology Association.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Socialist Prime Minister, Pedro Sánchez, has described the fires in dramatic terms, placing Spain in the front line of an environmental crisis.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The climate emergency kills," he said in July, during a visit to the southern province of Almería where a wildfire claimed 15 lives.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Research found that extreme heat and resulting fires in Spain were now 40 times more likely This year, around 300,000 hectares of land have been burned in Spain, according to the European Forest Fire Information System (EFFIS), approximately half the total affected in the entire European Union.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The local authorities in Castilla y León, the region most heavily affected by this year's massive fire near Madrid, are offering compensation – between €5,500 ($6,300; £4,700) and €25,000 ($29,000; £21,000) to each farmer – depending on the damage suffered.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: But Izquierdo estimates that this will cover less than half of his losses.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: For decades, Spain's warm climate has been a boon for one of its other biggest industries - tourism.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Sun-drenched resorts along the Mediterranean coast, and in the Balearic and Canary Islands, have driven the country's growth as a tourist hub.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: This year, close to 100 million foreigners are expected to come to Spain, making it the second most-visited country in the world, just behind France.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Yet there are signs that the heat is becoming too much for some travellers.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, this summer tested their tolerance of heat, with the country registering a record-breaking 61 days of heatwaves that continued into early September.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Toledo repeatedly saw temperatures in excess of 40C.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It's quite difficult to do the tours in the summer," says guide Diego Esteban, of the company Visit Toledo.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "We need to adapt, whether it is those of us who work in the tourism industry or the locals." When leading tours in the summer months, Esteban makes sure that there are frequent stops, drinking water is provided and that the itineraries include plenty of shade.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, he would like to see more shade and drinking fountains available.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: He says the heat has started to change the timing of the tourist season, bringing many more visitors during the cooler months of spring and autumn.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Warmer summers have also encouraged the so-called "coolcation" trend, whereby Spanish travellers seek out cooler areas to spend their holidays, typically in the north of the country.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Another consequence of Spain's warming climate has been drought.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: In 2024, after three years of minimal rainfall, the north-eastern region of Catalonia temporarily introduced stringent restrictions on water use, including a 25% reduction for industry and an 80% reduction for crop farming.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Heavy rainfall since then has lifted the restrictions, but the drought had a major impact on the local economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The most dramatic and tragic natural phenomenon Spain has seen in recent years were flash floods that killed 237 people in the east of the country in October 2024, centred on the Valencia region.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spanish meteorological research group Climatoc-Lab described it as "a manifestation of how global warming alters the hydrological cycle".
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: The Valencia Chamber of Commerce estimated that the floods caused €4.5bn in direct damage.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Thousands of businesses were affected, some literally washed away by the floodwater, while others were able to resume operations after a lengthy recovery.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "It was a disaster, both in terms of the lives lost and the impact on businesses, on workers, employers and ordinary people," says Laura Llácer Álvarez, manager of the Fepeval federation of industrial parks in the Valencia region.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Spain's geographical position, along with its climate and topography, make it unusually vulnerable as global temperatures increase.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Germanwatch, an independent environmental organisation, ranked Spain the world's 20th most affected country in its climate risk index for 2024, just behind Nigeria and Mali.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: Yet there are those who see an upside for the economy.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "Climate change affects how we produce, how we invest and how we consume," says Julián Cubero, head of economics of climate change at economic think tank BBVA Research.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: He points to how heat can act as a drag on economic activity.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "We all work worse when it's hot," he says.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: However, he adds, a greener economy can create new jobs with greater productivity.
sentences.article_title: Spain battles climate change on several fronts

sentences.text: "The key is to realise that if we don't act, growth will slow down, and if it's handled right it can become an opportunity," he says.

sentences.text: But there's a long way to go.

sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Once the optimum solution (known as a policy) is found, it can be uploaded and used by the hardware - in this case Freddo.

sentences.text: As they were starting from scratch Lu and Storey could optimise the software to exploit the powerful computer chips used in AI, known as graphics processing units or GPUs.

sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: These unexpected events could happen very quickly and the robot needs to be able to quickly adapt to ensure its actions remain safe and on-mission," Lu says.

sentences.text: Nvidia is at the other end of the industry.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It dominates the market for computer chips used for AI and has a leading robotics software division, with hundreds of engineers.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It does not build robots, instead it has a suite of software designed to let organisations train and control robots.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: That includes virtual simulation training systems and a so-called world model , external , called Cosmos, which gives a robot an understanding of the physics of the real world and how its environment might change as it moves around.

sentences.text: But even with the powerful computer resources available to Nvidia, the software only gives a rudimentary understanding of the real world.

sentences.text: "Manipulation, - where I just grab a bottle, that's not too hard.

sentences.text: But he's confident that good progress is being made.

sentences.text: "When we talk about creating the [virtual] world and actually scanning it in - a lot of that is actually manual labour.

sentences.text: "We're just throwing agents at it... it's basically given us a huge workforce," Huang says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Simulation is not the only method for training robots.

sentences.text: Rika Antonova has spent more than a decade working in robotics Rika Antonova has been working in the field of robotics since 2015 and is currently an associate professor at the Department of Computer Science and Technology at the University of Cambridge.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Her research is focused on , external developing software and hardware that can aid robots to learn complex behaviour.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: Antonova works with a training system called MuJoCo, owned by Google's DeepMind since 2021.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's open-source software, which means researchers can use it for free, and are allowed to tinker with the code.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "It is very, very user-friendly.

sentences.text: So for research groups or for small start-ups, that's useful," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: She says that Vsim's approach - very fast simulation - is promising.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "If you have a very, very fast simulator, then you can simulate hundreds of millions of samples in that few seconds that your robot is thinking about how to adjust its motion, and then you can change the motion almost in real time," she says.

sentences.text: But those simulated environments are still rough approximations of the real world, which limits what can be trained.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: "There are certain things that are hard to model in simulation, like highly deformable objects and cutting," she says.
sentences.article_title: The virtual worlds where robots are trained

sentences.text: It's a challenge that Nvidia and Lu and Storey at Vsim are working on.

sentences.article_title: New right to bereavement leave to cover step and half relatives

sentences.article_title: New right to bereavement leave to cover step and half relatives

sentences.text: Specialist courts to handle cases of rape and other sexual offences will be introduced across England and Wales over the next two years, the prime minister has announced.

sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.article_title: Specialist courts for rape cases to be rolled out in England and Wales

sentences.text: Health spokesperson Helen Morgan met parents and babies to discuss maternity care Liberal Democrats are calling for one-to-one midwife care for women in labour, as figures suggest life-altering childbirth injuries in England have reached record levels.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: Lib Dem analysis of NHS figures showed the number of women suffering potentially life-threatening levels of blood loss is the highest ever recorded in England.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: Three in every 100 women suffered serious tearing injuries requiring emergency surgery in the first half of this year, something party leader Sir Ed Davey said was a "devastating indictment of our NHS maternity services".
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: The government is expected to publish a new national maternity and neonatal action plan by the end of the year.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: Speaking to BBC Breakfast at the Lib Dem annual conference in Brighton, Davey pledged to spend £600m a year on maternity services if in government.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: He said £1.3bn a year was currently being spent on "failure" through negligence compensation payouts for poor maternity services, but said this investment should go towards prevention instead.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: Calling for more senior midwives and consultants, he said: "Our current maternity staff are run ragged - they're massively overstretched.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: "That's the best way, all the evidence shows, to make sure maternity units are safe," he added.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: "It is a scandal at the moment - we've seen inquiry after inquiry.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: So many women are suffering injuries at birth and we're seeing the loss of babies too; it is a tragedy as well as a scandal." He said ministers "cannot turn a blind eye to this national safety scandal" and mothers "deserve safe, compassionate care".
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: The Lib Dems are calling for a consultant obstetrician to be present on every labour ward at all hours, one-to-one midwifery care for every woman in labour, and recruit an extra 300 consultant midwives.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: The party pointed to Care Quality Commission (CQC) survey data showing one-in-10 women, about 54,000, were left alone during late stages of labour or childbirth last year, which the Lib Dems said was due to lack of training and staff shortages.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: More than 8,000 women had postpartum haemorrhages with blood loss of more than 1.5l since the start of this year, more than double the number over the equivalent period in 2021, the party's analysis of NHS figures suggests.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: Rates of major haemorrhage peaked between April and June this year, while 32.7 women per thousand needed emergency treatment.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: The rate of third or fourth degree vaginal tears during childbirth has risen by 29% in the last five years, according to the analysis.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: The Lib Dem health spokesperson Helen Morgan, who successfully campaigned for an independent maternity commissioner to drive improvements, said reports on previous maternity scandals were "gathering dust".
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: "Years after the Shrewsbury and Telford scandal which devastated my community - my neighbours and friends - women continue to suffer," she said.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: "This must be the moment we say 'enough'." A review in 2022 found catastrophic failures at Shrewsbury and Telford NHS Trust (SaTH) over 20 years may have led to the deaths of more than 200 babies.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: The trust apologised and said it had already put in measures to prevent a repeat.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: A Department of Health and Social Care (DHSC) spokesperson said the review to be published later this year will bring together the recommendations from the Baroness Amos, Donna Ockenden, and Lady Justice Thirlwall inquiries, set clear priorities and hold the system to account for delivering improved outcomes.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: "Every woman deserves safe maternity care and the new health secretary has made this issue a personal priority," they said.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: The DHSC is also extending Martha's Rule to every maternity and neonatal ward to ensure that any reports of deterioration from patients or their families are acted upon, and has invested £187m since April 2025 to address critical safety risks in the maternity and neonatal estate.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: "He never raised any objections to that decision at the time, and he has never apologised since.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: "We have grown really fast under my leadership , with record number of MPs and running more councils," he said.
sentences.article_title: Lib Dems call for one-to-one midwife care during childbirth

sentences.text: Andy Burnham has hailed a deal between Denmark and the US to "strengthen security in the Arctic" after the two countries resolved a months-long feud over Greenland.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: The UK prime minister and his Danish counterpart Mette Frederiksen "welcomed the US's commitment to the region" in a call on Sunday morning, Downing Street said.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: Nato previously said the agreement would help stabilise the region, while Trump declared Denmark would grant the US "permanent control over security, and all other needs" in the semi-autonomous Danish territory in the Arctic.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: Burnham's comments come as he is expected to meet Trump for the first time at the UN General Assembly (UNGA) in New York this week.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: Nato welcomes Greenland deal as Trump says it will give US 'permanent security control' The agreement comes after months of threats by Trump to "take" Greenland over national security concerns, citing its strategic Arctic location for defence purposes as well as its mineral wealth.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: No text of the agreement has been released, but Trump said in a Truth Social post that the deal came with "no cost to the United States" and meant it could "do what is necessary" to "secure and defend the security of Greenland".
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: He said it included a rule that no US adversary could maintain a military presence in Greenland or "make sensitive investments in Greenland, without our express written approval".
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: A No 10 spokesperson said in a readout of Sunday's phone call that Burnham and Frederiksen "welcomed the US's commitment to the region and underlined the strategic and shared importance of the High North for Euro-Atlantic security".
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: "So let Donald Trump try to pretend he's had a victory.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: The truth is, Europe, Nato, countries like Canada stood up to him and won." Trump had for months threatened to purchase or annex the semi-autonomous territory, arguing that it was vulnerable to adversaries, including Russia and China.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: Following the announcement of the deal, Frederiksen said she was "pleased that there is a prospect of a good agreement" for all three parties, which was expected to be signed at the UN General Assembly next week.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: The deal "strengthens our common security in the Arctic and the North Atlantic area" while also recognising "the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the kingdom and the right of the Greenlandic people to self-determination", she said in a joint statement with Greenland's Prime Minister Jens-Frederik Nielsen.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: The agreement would still need to go through "the necessary parliamentary procedures to enter into force" once signed, the statement noted.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: Burnham has spoken to Trump at least twice since entering Downing Street and No 10 said he intended to use the UNGA to "drive forward work on issues that matter to people at home", including the cost of living and the war in Ukraine.
sentences.article_title: Burnham hails Greenland deal ahead of expected first Trump meeting

sentences.text: Eric Fawley said he had been drawing since he was five years old A 94-year-old man with dementia said he was "very happy" to be given the opportunity to have his artwork exhibited in the House of Commons.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: Eric Fawley, from Blackpool, has produced hundreds of drawings since arriving at Greenbanks Care Home in Watford, Hertfordshire, over a year ago, after a fire at his home.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: His drawings and paintings depict the world around him, as well as his former bosses at BT.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: The exhibition was facilitated by the Watford Labour MP Matt Turmaine after he saw Fawley's work at the care home.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: This is one of the few drawings Fawley has produced in colour, as he prefers to sketch in black and white Fawley said he began creating artworks from an early age, encouraged by his mother, a violinist, and his father, a gifted amateur painter.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: His family were unable to support his ambition to attend art school.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: He left school at the age of 14 and worked in a variety of jobs, including electrical work for the famous Blackpool illuminations, before going on to become a Post Office engineer with BT.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: Singhvi ensures Fawley's artwork is framed and displayed for residents and staff at the care home Fawley relocated to London, after he married his wife Olive, and he continued to work for the telecoms company.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: From there, he rose through the ranks of the company, taking charge of an office where his portraits and keenly observed caricatures of colleagues were prominently displayed.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: Fawley said he enjoyed "sending up colleagues" and that they "secretly used to like it".
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: When drawing someone, he said it was important to start with their hair.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: "If the hair is wrong, then everything is wrong," he added.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: Fawley's sketches of former colleagues at BT won him several art competitions.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: One of Fawley's wartime sketches features his sister, Charlotte, who regularly visits him at the care home Since moving to Greenbanks in March last year, Fawley has continued to sketch.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: He said being creative helped to focus his mind and "ensures that every day is different".
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: He has held exhibitions across Essex and also performed a ceremonial ribbon-cutting at an exhibition at Harlow Library.
sentences.article_title: Artist, 94, thrilled by House of Commons exhibition

sentences.text: Staff at the care home are "super proud of him" and are "excited" to see his artwork gain wider recognition, with Fawley challenging perceptions of what people can achieve in care.

sentences.text: Children as young as 13 are getting ketamine bladder damage, doctors running the UK's first and only dedicated NHS clinic for it have told the BBC in an exclusive interview.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Medics at Alder Hey Hospital in Liverpool say some patients - they have had over 100 referrals since opening last May - describe 'peeing a jellyfish', which is some of the bladder's protective lining being shed.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Prolonged damage can lead to incontinence or uncontrolled peeing, and even kidney failure.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Many children at the clinic had been taking ketamine for a year or more, meaning some may have started when they were 12 or younger.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Some with emotional trauma say the ketamine, sold for pocket money prices, helps "shush" or quieten their brain.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Ketamine's most common form is white or pale-brown grainy powder that is often inhaled (snorted) or sometimes injected by users.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: It can be a liquid or a crystal form too.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: The drug is a general anaesthetic so it reduces or blunts sensations in the body.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Users say it can make them feel dream-like and detached, chilled and relaxed.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: But it can also cause extreme harm.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Prof Rachel Isba who runs the clinic told the BBC some of the children she has seen had started wetting the bed or having to go to the toilet more often and in a hurry.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: "Sometimes they don't always make it.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: They might have accidents...and a lot of them report pain in their bladder.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: "They describe this feeling of weeing over broken glass.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: It's very painful." She says, unfortunately, some of them will use the ketamine to treat the pain.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: "Ketamine is a very good pain reliever.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: It's an anaesthetic, and so they get into a vicious cycle or 'K loop', which makes their bladder worse," says Isba.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: She says ketamine is very cheap, "pocket-money level".
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: "And you only need a small amount to feel an effect." She says some children find it hard to quit if their mates are still doing it.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: "There's use going on at school.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: And, unfortunately for many of these children they are not able to attend education for various reasons." Some had pre-existing conditions like ADHD, while others had been in and out of the care system.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Ketamine abuse in children and young people is on the rise in the UK.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: The Alder Hey doctors , external saw one young patient in 2023, nine in 2024, and then "a rapid escalation" in 2025, which led them to open the bespoke clinic in May.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: They get about one referral every week from GPs or emergency departments in Cheshire, Merseyside and other nearby regions.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Of the first 60 they saw, 43 were girls.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Despite its name, "ketamine bladder" can affect the entire urinary tract, including the kidneys and ureters.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Symptoms include an urgent and frequent need to urinate.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: This can be very painful and the pee can be blood-stained.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Although stopping using ketamine can help, sometimes the damage can be so serious that the bladder needs surgical repair or even removal.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Some users experience abdominal pain and spasms, or "K cramps" too.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: There are reports that heavy users are getting liver damage, but it is difficult to separate harms from other things people may also be taking, including other street drugs and alcohol.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Isba says cannabis and alcohol are still more popular, but ketamine is "probably up into third place".
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Children at the clinic often say they have also tried other drugs, drank alcohol, and vaped.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: About three out of every 10 people who frequently use ketamine get bladder issues, says the British Association of Urological Surgeons , external .
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Sometimes it is reversible, if the drug use stops.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Given the risks, there have been calls to reclassify it as a Class A drug - like cocaine and heroin - but the Advisory Council on the Misuse of Drugs has recommended to government that ketamine should remain a Class B controlled substance, like amphetamines and cannabis.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Isba says children are disadvantaged when it comes to accessing services.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: "There are definitely some children out there who are under the age of 16 who if they were 18 would be offered an inpatient detox stay.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: But because we don't have those facilities in the UK, they are not able to access that and that feels unfair.
sentences.article_title: Child ketamine users getting bladder damage describe 'peeing a jellyfish'

sentences.text: Particularly for the ones who are ready to stop." sentences.text: Burnham said it "feels very fitting" to welcome Martin as the first international visitor to Number 10 North Ireland's relationship with the UK under Andy Burnham's premiership has got off to a "very good start", Taoiseach (Irish prime minister) Micheál Martin has said.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: But he refused to be drawn on how much the issue of Irish unity had featured during their first official meeting at Number 10 North on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: The visit came days after US President Donald Trump made comments about supporting a "unified Ireland".
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: Martin said the men had a "broad discussion" about upholding the Good Friday Agreement and that they did not get into specifics.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: "It was the first meeting, it went well...
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: I think we have the capacity to make a lot of progress on a lot of issues in the time ahead," he said.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: Martin was the first international leader to visit the government's new headquarters in Manchester, and also visited the Brian Boru Irish Club in Burnham's constituency in Ashton-in-Makerfield.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: On his visit to Northern Ireland last month, Burnham said a border poll was " off the table ", but later said he stood by the Good Friday Agreement.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: The taoiseach and prime minister visited the Brian Boru Irish Club in Ashton-in-Makerfield The taoiseach said he and the prime minister had discussed the UK's Troubles legacy legislation in depth, and that he had "stressed the importance" of passing the bill through Parliament.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: The government is expected to publish details of changes in the middle of next month, with Martin saying both London and Dublin had been working closely on it.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: He also said both he and the prime minister wanted to see the power-sharing institutions at Stormont working more effectively, and that the Irish government believes there needs to be reform.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: He said Burnham understood the issue and was currently focused on trying to resolve negotiations with the Stormont executive to agree a budget for this year.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: Burnham said the relationship between the UK and Ireland matters "on every single level" as he greeted the taoiseach on Friday.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: The prime minister said they were "working together" to uphold the principles of the peace deal for Northern Ireland.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: Burnham added that as "co-custodians of the Good Friday Agreement, we are working together to uphold its principles as we approach the 30th anniversary".
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'

sentences.text: The Good Friday Agreement, also known as the Belfast Agreement, was a political deal designed to bring an end to 30 years of violent conflict in Northern Ireland, known as the Troubles.
sentences.article_title: Ireland's relationship with UK under Burnham off to 'very good start'
