sentences.text: If you see someone you think has heat exhaustion , the NHS says you should: , external move them to a cool place get them to lie down and raise their feet slightly get them to drink plenty of water - sports or rehydration drinks are also OK cool their skin - spray or sponge them with cool water and fan them.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Cold packs around the armpits or neck are also good If they can be cooled down within half an hour, then heat exhaustion is not normally serious.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: However, if they do not recover within 30 minutes, then they are at risk of heatstroke .
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: This is a medical emergency and you should call 999 immediately.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: People with heatstroke may stop sweating even though they are too hot.

sentences.text: What to do if you think someone has heat exhaustion or heatstroke People who are older or have some long-term conditions - such as heart disease -  are sometimes less able to cope with the strain heat puts on the body.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Diabetes can make the body lose water more quickly and some complications of the disease can alter blood vessels and the ability to sweat.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Children and those who are less mobile may also be more vulnerable.

sentences.text: Brain diseases, such as dementia, can also leave people unaware of the heat or unable to do anything about it.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: People who are homeless will also be more exposed to the sun.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: In high temperatures, they increase the dangers of dehydration and imbalances in key minerals in the body.

sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: During 2022 - which saw the highest recorded temperature in England at 40.3C - there were an estimated 2,985 so-called "excess deaths" as a result of the heat , external , the most recorded in any given year.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: There were an estimated 1,311 heat-associated deaths , external during summer 2024, and an estimated 1,504 , external during summer 2025.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: Most heat-related excess deaths are due to heart attacks and strokes caused by the strain of trying to keep body temperatures stable.

sentences.text: The higher death rate starts to kick in once the thermometer passes 25C-26C.
sentences.article_title: What does hot weather do to the body?

sentences.text: However, evidence suggests the deaths tend to be caused by higher temperatures in spring or early summer rather than during "peak summer".

sentences.text: The evidence from previous heatwaves is the increase in deaths happens very quickly - within the first 24 hours of a heatwave.

sentences.text: University applicants in England will be given clearer information about student loans before they take them out, the government has said.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Ministers said they would spell out that governments can change repayment rules and that different career choices can affect how much borrowers repay.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: They agreed to some but not all of the recommendations made by MPs after an inquiry into student loans, and did not say whether they would reverse a freeze to the repayment threshold for some graduates.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The inquiry found the way loans had been presented to teenagers amounted to mis-selling , after the BBC revealed the Department for Education (DfE) had compared repayments to £30-a-month phone contracts.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The recent debate has centred around Plan 2 loans, which were issued in England between September 2012 and July 2023, and are still issued in Wales.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The interest rate on those loans is the Retail Prices Index (RPI) measure of inflation plus up to 3% depending on earnings, and borrowers repay at a rate of 9% of everything they earn over a repayment threshold, which is meant to rise with inflation every year.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The loans are written off after 30 years.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Campaigners want a lower interest rate, a lower repayment rate and for the government to reverse a decision last year to freeze the threshold at £29,385 for three years in England.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Freezing that threshold means graduates start repaying their loans sooner and, once they do, they pay more than they would have done if it had risen with inflation.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: MPs on the Treasury Committee called for a U-turn on that decision as part of a series of recommendations after an inquiry this summer.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: It also said "more can be done to help student loan borrowers understand how their loan balance may change over the long term".
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The government also said giving students long-term predictions of how much they might ultimately repay risked being "misleading" because of "limited" accuracy.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: It proposed instead to "demonstrate how different life and career choices may affect repayment trajectories", including salary progression, retraining, part-time work, and career breaks.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Nick Hillman, director of the Higher Education Policy Institute, who helped design the Plan 2 system, said the government had "absolutely rejected" most of what the Treasury Committee had recommended and its response would not meet the concerns of Plan 2 graduates.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Oliver Gardner, founder of the Rethink Repayment campaign, said the government's response "does not go far enough" and he wanted to see "concrete action" in the autumn Budget.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: While Dame Meg Hillier, chair of the Treasury Committee, said making information clearer was "an important step" but "doesn't help graduates who are angry that they didn't receive the same service and are now facing punitive repayment terms on a loan which keeps growing".
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: She urged the chancellor to reverse the threshold freeze in this autumn's Budget.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: In March, a BBC investigation found that as well as comparing monthly student loan repayments to phone contracts, the government told presenters to "avoid words [or] phrases like debt" during presentations in schools across England a decade ago.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: More than 120 MPs and peers recently signed a letter coordinated by the campaign group Rethink Repayment calling for an "urgent review" of the system.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: One of the signatories, Liberal Democrat MP Tom Gordon, who is a Plan 2 borrower, is set to introduce a bill calling for a review in Parliament next week.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Education Secretary Lucy Powell has previously said the interest rate on Plan 2 loans was "egregious" and the issue was at the top of her in-tray.
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: The Student Loans Company said it was working with the government to "provide clear, relatable and trusted guidance".
sentences.article_title: Student loan terms to be made clearer in England

sentences.text: Martine Barons who began lifting weights during lockdown is now a three-time world champion A 65-year-old grandmother has become a three-time world champion powerlifter after only starting the sport two and a half years ago.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Martine Barons, from Stratford-upon-Avon, said she began lifting weights during lockdown after listening to a seminar that said women going through menopause should run less and lift more.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Her colleague at the University of Warwick, who is also a personal trainer, then showed Barons how to deadlift, and spotted her potential.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons is now nicknamed The Deadlifting Grandma.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: On Monday, she won at the AWPC World Powerlifting Championships in the 65 to 85 age group, becoming a three-time world champion, after starting out entering competitions just for fun.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons said she has seen a "huge change" in her physique and capabilities "I have seen such a huge change in my own physique and my capabilities – I am sure that my body is at least 20 years younger," she told BBC CWR.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "When they invited me to the British and European Championships, I thought, 'Well I have been invited it would be rude not to go', but who thought it would lead to this?
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Barons said her journey, down to hard work and dedication over the past couple of years, has been "so exciting".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "I have learnt so much, I have met people all around the world, and it has been delightful," she said.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: For women who want to get fit and improve their strength, Baron said there were lots of options, one route is to join a gym and develop a tailored programme with a coach.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Alternatively, Baron said those who prefer more privacy could "start really gently at home with some resistance bands and a programme".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: She added her powerlifting has led to having more capability on a day-to-day basis, along with now being able to touch her toes first thing in the morning.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "If I need to move furniture at home, I can do that, I can toss my grandchildren in the air, I can play games with them," she said.
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: "My posture is better and I just feel more capable and more confident in everyday life".
sentences.article_title: The Deadlifting Grandma: 'I'm a world champion'

sentences.text: Sara Kahsai wants all survivors of FGM to seek help and not suffer alone Sara Kahsai grew up in Sudan but moved to Birmingham, England, in 2022 after marrying a bus driver from the city.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: But as she settled into married life and her new home, she was coming to terms with a life-changing discovery.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Sara realised she was a victim-survivor of Female Genital Mutiliation (FGM), a procedure she had endured as a young girl.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: She was floored by the revelation and, not least, the excruciating pain she was now beginning to fully understand.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "The shock was massive," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "It made it difficult with my physical relationship with my husband - but he was very kind and very patient with me." Warning: This story contains descriptions of the practices involved in female genital mutilation Sara turned to the one person she knew must have orchestrated it - her mother - and asked her why.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It was the culture to do it for everybody," she said her mother, still living in Africa, told her.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "When I spoke to my mum she was really upset and she apologised to me." FGM involves the partial or total removal of female genitalia for non-medical reasons, and is practiced in some parts of Africa, the Middle East and Asia.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It also happens within some migrant communities in the UK, where it is illegal and treated as child abuse.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It is also against the law to take a girl abroad for FGM.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Reasons include social acceptance, religion, misconceptions about hygiene and preserving a girl or woman's virginity.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The Home Office website cites World Health Organisation figures showing three million girls undergo some form , external of the procedure every year in Africa alone.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The mum received help for her FGM after she found out she was pregnant When Sara fell pregnant, she finally told health professionals she had endured FGM as a child.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: She was immediately referred to the specialist FGM Clinic, run by midwives at Birmingham Women's Hospital.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Midwife Renata Hanif deals with around 200 cases each year and says her job is to ensure the wellbeing of women and safeguard unborn children.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "Some types of female circumcision can affect the vaginal delivery," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: They offer deinfibulation - a procedure that can be carried out during pregnancy to separate fused tissue and enable safer births.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: What is FGM, where does it happen and why?
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Victim-survivors of FGM can also experience difficulty with urinating and menstruating, the midwife said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Women are more prone to infections and sepsis, and can suffer from severe and ongoing pain, as well having to deal with psychological trauma, anxiety and depression.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Many patients find it hard to talk to her about what's happened to them, Hanif said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "It is very difficult, very emotional.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It's very difficult for the woman to actually come forward and to come to the clinic, attend the clinic, and have a conversation with me as well," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "I explain to them that I'm here to help and I try to explain to them what happened to them when they were a child." She said most women leave the clinic with a better understanding of how they have been affected and how they can take back control of their bodies.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "We talk about every part, what that part is there for and what's been removed and what cause for concern and what effect this will have for the rest of her life," Hanif said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Counselling is also offered as well as information on how partners and husbands can support them.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Midwife Renata Hanif runs the FGM centre at Birmingham Women's Hospital In 2015, children's charity Barnardo's set up the National FGM Centre to help better protect women and girls.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It works to prevent FGM, raise awareness of it and support those affected.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: The centre said schools are legally required to teach pupils about FGM and the law surrounding it as part of relationships and sex education.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: But how it is delivered can vary between schools.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: It's also not mandatory for it to be taught in primary schools and they want to see that change.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "For us, a huge part of tackling FGM is prevention," Rohma Ullah, from the centre, said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Among improvements on the way are new guidelines to help identify girls at risk of being taken abroad for FGM.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: Sara wants to urge other women in a similar position to take immediate action.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "I have a message to all ladies who've had FGM," she said.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "When they come to the UK it is different.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: There's help here - go to their GP, seek help, ask for help.
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: "If I knew I could seek help I would not have waited until I was expecting... because I did suffer a lot before." If you have been affected by the contents of the article, support is available through the BBC Action Line website .
sentences.article_title: 'My mother apologised': A survivor's journey after genital mutilation

sentences.text: English pupils have pulled ahead of the rest of the UK in international reading, maths and science tests, new data suggests, with Scotland and Wales falling further behind.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The 2025 Programme for International Student Assessment (Pisa) saw reading and maths scores slump in each UK nation except England, while all four saw an uptick in science, with that rise again most notable in England.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The latest Pisa report, which is published every three years, also warned of a worldwide decline in teenagers' reading skills.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Teenagers were losing the skills that "matter most in the age of AI", such as being able to critically evaluate information from different sources, it said.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The share of "hasty readers", who rush through texts to give quick, incorrect answers, has almost doubled between 2018 and 2025.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The report warned the fall was greatest in those from "relatively well off" families.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Run by the Organisation for Economic Cooperation and Development (OECD), the Pisa tests assess teenagers on their ability to solve problems, think critically and communicate, before asking them a wider range of questions about their education in a questionnaire.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Although the UK performed well overall, the rankings varied significantly again, with results showing England, where the curriculum is significantly different, pulling consistently ahead of Northern Ireland, Scotland and Wales.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: England's schools minister, Georgia Gould, said the government wanted to "build on" the positive results and "go further so all young people leave school with strong literacy and numeracy".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The 2025 Pisa tests were taken by a sample of 760,000 15-year-olds in 91 countries.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: In the UK, where education differs between the home nations, 15,566 students took the tests in 515 schools.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: In England, where it was recently announced that technical subjects would soon be available to students from age 14 , Gould held up high-performing Estonia as an example of where "academic excellence can go hand in hand with high-quality vocational routes".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: "Our reforms will build on England's strong academic foundations so future generations not only perform well, but feel connected to school and excited about where their education can take them," she added.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: But Laura Trott, England's shadow education secretary, said the country's successes were down to previous reforms, and accused the new government of trying to "sabotage" them.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Wales falls further behind rest of UK in international school tests Primary teachers hired to teach Glasgow secondary pupils to read While Wales lags behind the rest of the UK overall, on science it is ahead of other European countries such as France, Spain and the Netherlands.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: As the tests last year were taken by 15-year-olds, the results there largely reflect learning under an old curriculum, which has recently been changed.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Anna Brychan, Wales' minister for education and Welsh language, said plans were in place to support schools, adding that the results "highlight our need to improve standards of reading and maths, as a priority".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Scotland's education secretary, Mairi McAllan, said the results showed "real strengths in Scottish education, as well as areas we're already working to improve".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: But Scottish Labour said results had "flatlined since 2022's historically poor results", while the Scottish Liberal Democrats said the education system under the SNP had "tumbled down the rankings, lagging behind England on every measure of performance".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Northern Ireland's education minister, Paul Givan, said pupils there had performed well by international standards, but that - like other countries - its education system was facing "significant challenges", adding that "there is much more work to do".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Overall, the Pisa tests provide the biggest global snapshot of education systems and an independent view of how teenagers are performing compared with their peers in other countries, so it is a relative measure.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Andreas Schleicher, director of education at the OECD, said reading was the "mother of all skills" and that the steep decline was a concern.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: He said children's ability to read complex texts had declined by the equivalent of "two school years" in the last decade.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Longer-term Pisa research suggested students who read longer books performed best, he added, as it helped them to learn to hold complex information in mind.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Schools like Meadow Park, in Coventry, are adopting a range of approaches to improve pupils' reading skills, including weekly book club discussions led by tutors.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Year 10 pupil Ampaabeng said the sessions have had a "really positive impact" on his reading since they were brought in a year ago.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The school has also invested in a wider range of books in the library, where reading for pleasure at lunchtime is encouraged.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: A mobile phone ban was introduced at the school two years ago to reduce distractions - an approach which is commended by the new report.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: "In a digital age, it's easier to pick up a phone than it is a book," head teacher Bernadette Pettman said.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: She said reading together had enabled the school to "break down that fear of reading" and that pupils had "absolutely embraced it".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: Bernadette Pettman says the school tries to make reading fun with book clubs, creative writing sessions and visits from authors One of the other big changes in education, picked up in the OECD's report, is the use of AI.
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: It warns that excessive use can lead to pupils avoiding looking up information themselves, a process sometimes called "cognitive off-loading".
sentences.article_title: England up in reading, maths and science rankings as Scotland and Wales fall behind

sentences.text: The BBC spoke to parents and experts to find out their back-to-school tips It's back-to-school time again - and families brace for the challenge of swapping summer lie-ins for school routines, easing first-day nerves and getting ready for the year ahead.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: While children in Scotland returned to school in mid-August, children in England, Wales and Northern Ireland will be returning in the coming week as September begins.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: We spoke to experts to find out their six key tips to make going back to school as stress-free as possible.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Cerys Parker, a teacher and blogger, says one of the best ways to keep organised during school time is to keep a consistent morning routine.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Her morning starts 30 minutes before her children wake up, for some alone time and a hot coffee.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She  then makes them the same breakfast every morning, which they eat together with no screens, then it's upstairs for showers and getting ready for school.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker also keeps copies of her children's timetables so she knows what to prepare on specific days, such as when they have PE She grabs their lunch boxes and they leave the house at 07:30 for the bus, or 07:50 if Parker is dropping them at school on the way to her own job.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: The night before, she makes sure school bags are packed, shoes are ready, uniform is laid out and lunch is packed for the morning.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "We have things in the same place, so the bags are always in the same location, the keys, and that makes the morning smoother.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: There's no panic about where everything's going to be." It is easy to forget non-uniform days, sports days or study sessions.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Parker recommends having a family calendar pinned to your wall or your fridge - somewhere you can easily see it every day.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's an academic year calendar with a space for each of us, and then an events section, so as soon as a notice comes in, I write it down." This could include things like meal plans, after-school activities or - depending on your child's age - exams.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: After school, many children are tired and are not up for discussion about their day, so Will Shield, professor of child and educational psychology at the University of Exeter, suggests changing your approach to the conversation.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask some open questions, instead of interrogating them," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Ask what made you smile today?
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Or who did you play with at lunchtime?" These sorts of questions are a lot easier to answer for a child, he says, instead of asking what they did.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "See it as part of the process of separating and loving you, missing you, which is really important." Many families will have children attending school for the first time, which can be just as big a moment for parents as it is for new pupils.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Shield says parents should "reassure themselves" about the routine they will need to follow on school mornings.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Visit the school, walk or drive past it, bring bedtimes back a bit earlier so it's not just a big start in the first week," he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's about much more basic things, like feeling comfortable and safe to be in a classroom with other children," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Building independence can also help bridge the gap between home and school life, she says, by encouraging your child to do some things by themselves, such as zipping up their own coat.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "It's just building that sense of, I'm ready to do this without you," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: But Deiros Collado also stresses that your child should be able to ask for help when they need it.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "One of the best skills you can give your little ones is being able to say to an adult, 'Help me,' because you want your kid to be able to say that to a teacher." She also suggests a "goodbye ritual" with your child to practise separation, such as blowing a kiss.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Katharine Radice says that focusing too much on the homework outcome you want for your child can be "demotivating" for them Katharine Radice, teacher and author, recommends putting together a homework timetable.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Doing this puts boundaries around homework and makes it easier to ring-fence distraction-free time," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: This could be different every week depending on different activities, but Radice stresses there should be a plan in advance so it's not left to the last minute.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: For supporting children with homework, Radice suggests approaching the task in a "positive and open way" and listening to what they might be finding difficult.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: She also recommends looking for opportunities to praise your child's effort in doing work to help them "stay motivated." "If your child thinks their outcomes won't meet your expectations, they may start to feel that their effort is pointless," she says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: Some children who are returning to school may have anxieties about the year ahead, and Shield recommends to sit with your child and listen to their concerns.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "Don't immediately reassure them by saying, 'You'll be fine,'" he says.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: "The child's got no evidence they will be fine because they're worried." He suggests phrases such as "I can see you're worried" to make a child feel listened to.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: It is also worth trying to dig deeper to find out what is making them worried about school specifically.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: He also recommends some gentle encouragement of positive things they like about school to ease some worries, such as lunchtime or playing sports with friends.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: If anxiety does become overwhelming for them, if they aren't sleeping or it is stopping them from doing everyday things, then Shield recommends talking to the school or a local GP.
sentences.article_title: Six ways parents could make the return to school a little easier

sentences.text: King Charles has warned AI executives of the "existential dangers" posed by the technology falling into the wrong hands.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: He made the comments at a summit he had convened at Dumfries House in Ayrshire to discuss how the tech can be used to benefit society.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: Those gathered at the meeting also included Kanishka Narayan, the UK's AI Minister, the Pope's advisor, and participants from AI giants such as Nvidia, OpenAI and Anthropic.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: It comes amid a series of recent warnings from people inside the industry about the rapidly evolving capabilities of advanced or "frontier" AI models and the regulation needed to keep them in check.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: "Those who have created these technologies are now increasingly warning that AI risks developing darker capacities - perhaps even to take life," the King told the executives.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: He said there seemed to be an "urgency" in "adequately considering the existential dangers of such technologies falling into the wrong hands, and being used in potentially catastrophic ways".
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: "The task before you is not merely to advance technology, but to ensure that it remains firmly in the service of humanity, community and the natural world," he told the group.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: The summit has been called to consider whether a "shared set of principles" can be developed to "help guide the future application" of AI.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: Jensen Huang, chief executive of Nvidia, was among top industry leaders attending.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: Nvidia is a central player in AI infrastructure, supplying chips to leading AI model developers including OpenAI and Meta.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: It is also the world's most valuable company, with a stock market value of around $5.15tn.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: Huang told the room he believed safety was "paramount", adding that companies should hold back a product and "keep engineering" if it was not safe enough.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: The Nvidia boss also highlighted the value of open models - systems which give users direct access to the software - as a way to "ensure that people and countries are not left behind".
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: He said these systems must also be protected so "researchers, universities, start-ups and countries" can develop applications "none of us would have imagined alone".
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: "Let us lead with responsible optimism, build AI safely and securely, open it to more people, expand our ambition and solve the problems that matter to the world," Huang added.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: Meanwhile Sir Demis Hassabis, who co-founded the UK AI lab DeepMind - later acquired by Google - offered a more cautious view on the pace of development.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: He said artificial general intelligence - systems it is believed could be as good as or better than humans at multiple tasks - was "probably only a few short years away" and could have an impact "ten times that of the Industrial Revolution".
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: The chance of something going wrong was "definitely non-zero", Sir Demis added.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: But he advocated for "a sensible middle way", saying humanity could address risks if collectively given the space and time to mitigate them.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: "The future is not yet written," he told the King's delegates.
sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.article_title: King Charles warns of 'existential danger' of AI falling into wrong hands

sentences.text: Researchers from Britain, Italy and Madagascar have spent years studying how indri lemurs use song to communicate A species of lemur known for its song appears to use a similar technique to opera singers, researchers have found.
sentences.article_title: Madagascar's singing lemurs use opera technique, study finds

sentences.text: Scientists from the University of Warwick, the University of Turin and the indri lemurs' home nation Madagascar have spent a number of years watching the species .
sentences.article_title: Madagascar's singing lemurs use opera technique, study finds

sentences.text: They have produced a new study which finds the lemurs open their mouths wider to reach higher notes - similar to a trained soprano.
sentences.article_title: Madagascar's singing lemurs use opera technique, study finds

sentences.text: Dr Chiara De Gregorio, honorary research fellow at the University of Warwick, said the animals had shown "the kind of fine-tuned coordination between voice and body that we usually associate with trained human singers, not with a lemur singing from the forest canopy".
sentences.article_title: Madagascar's singing lemurs use opera technique, study finds

sentences.text: "Every time the pitch of an indri's song rose, we could see its mouth opening wider, frame by frame," she said.
sentences.article_title: Madagascar's singing lemurs use opera technique, study finds

sentences.text: It is the first direct evidence of this kind of vocal-tract coordination in a non-human primate, according to the researchers.
sentences.article_title: Madagascar's singing lemurs use opera technique, study finds

sentences.text: The team behind the study of Madagascan lemurs has previously said their work could give a greater insight into how humans evolved to create music.
sentences.article_title: Madagascar's singing lemurs use opera technique, study finds

sentences.text: Another study, published in 2025, found young lemurs learned to sing in a similar manner to human children .
sentences.article_title: Madagascar's singing lemurs use opera technique, study finds

sentences.text: Scientists filmed a number of lemurs and then analysed their mouth movements The new study includes evidence that wild indris coordinate their mouth opening with the frequency of their songs, allowing them to amplify the sound.
sentences.article_title: Madagascar's singing lemurs use opera technique, study finds

sentences.text: This is known as formant tuning, and is widely used by professional singers to maximise the power of their voices.
sentences.article_title: Madagascar's singing lemurs use opera technique, study finds

sentences.text: Researchers studying indris believe the primates may use the technique for a similar purpose - to make their songs carry further in the thick forest.
sentences.article_title: Madagascar's singing lemurs use opera technique, study finds

sentences.text: Although humans and indris share a common ancestor approximately 74 million years ago, the scientists believe the techniques to project sound were developed independently.

sentences.text: David Etor's first break came after designing and building a kind of "solar oven" in Nigeria A Nigerian man has shared the story of how he rose up out of "abject poverty" as a child, to become one of the leading UK academics in his field.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: David Etor, 43, who grew up in Nigeria, only learned to read and write aged 12 and was told as a child that "nothing good will come out of you", but is now a lecturer in the School of Electrical, Electronic and Mechanical Engineering at the University of Bristol.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: He told the BBC how his family was so poor growing up that his mum would pretend to cook food in a kitchen they shared with others, "to protect our dignity" in front of neighbours.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "I didn't see a way out," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: Speaking to John Darvall on BBC Radio Bristol about the publication of his memoir, Etor described growing up in a "compound" with several other families, all sharing a single kitchen, toilet and bathroom.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "It was a very poor neighbourhood.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: We were particularly very poor that the poor neighbours would refer to us as poor," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "I do remember that there was a time where my mum would boil water.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "[She would] go back in and out, lift the lid, stir the water, go back into the room [and] come back as though she was preparing food...
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "She would come back in with that pot of water after a couple of hours and it will be as though she's just finished cooking a meal, but it was just water.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: To solve the problem, he designed and built a kind of "solar oven".
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "It worked incredibly well," he said, which led to an award from the state government and a job.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: That subsequently led him to receive a scholarship to study electrical power at Newcastle University and a PhD at Durham University, before he secured his current job in Bristol.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: Sir Steve Webb, the former MP and Pensions Minister, who got to know Etor through the church in Bristol, called his achievements "remarkable".
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "David's message is very much that people shouldn't be defined by their upbringing or their background," he said.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: "They shouldn't be written off." "I was pinching myself on my way here this morning," Etor added.
sentences.article_title: Nigerian academic on rags to riches: 'Nothing good was supposed to come out of me'

sentences.text: The Mercator projection is the map widely used across the globe but inaccurately depicts the sizes of countries and continents The UN has just called for the predominant world map to be replaced with one that more accurately reflects the true size of continents such as Africa.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The "Correct the Map" resolution adopted by the General Assembly aims to fix the discrepancy with the Mercator map, in which the African continent is shown as being of similar size to Greenland - even though it is in reality about 14 times larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN adopted a new map, the Equal Earth projection, which better represents the true sizes of landmasses - but comes with problems of its own.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: There have been many prominent attempts over the years to solve the problem of accurately representing the surface of a sphere on a flat rectangle, each with its own benefits and drawbacks.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Mercator projection has been around since the 16th Century and was vital for navigating the oceans The now widely used Mercator map was created in 1569 by Flemish cartographer Gerardus Mercator.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Its main purpose was to help European sailors navigate the oceans, as cartography Professor James Cheshire at University College London explained.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "He wanted a straight line to be drawn on a map to look like a straight line in reality if you followed a compass bearing," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "That was what it was intended to do, and that's what it does brilliantly well." To keep those angles correct on a flat map, Mercator had to stretch the grid lines wider as they moved away from the equator toward the poles.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: His map accommodates for the curvature of the Earth by making countries near the equator seem much smaller than they are and countries nearer the poles appear stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The distortion is a result of it being impossible to accurately represent the surface of a globe on a two-dimensional chart.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: More than 450 years on, Mercator's creation is still the basis for many of the maps we see in classrooms, on TV and online, including Google Maps.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But critics of the Mercator map say there is a psychological effect to viewing some places as smaller than they actually are and others as larger, as we instinctively view bigger things as more important.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: For Kenyan geographer Kioko Muendo, this has implicitly downplayed Africa's vast resources, population and investment opportunities.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "Maps are more than just guides for travellers - they shape how regions are perceived politically and economically," he told the BBC.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Equal Earth map aims to represent landmasses' area more fairly The Equal Earth map aims to address this problem with the Mercator projection.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It was developed by a team of cartographers in 2018 to present the size and shape of landmasses more accurately, and was inspired by the 1963 Robinson projection - a map that shows the entire globe's surface at once.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: As a result, the Equal Earth map was adopted by African Union members in February, before it was adopted by the UN.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But it sacrifices the straight lines that made the Mercator projection perfect for navigating with - and it cannot be used for measuring the true distance between different places.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: "You can preserve area, or you can preserve shape, or you can preserve distance and direction, but not everything at once perfectly, because otherwise you'd be back to a sphere," Cheshire said.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The Peters map projection gives a fairer idea of land area but distorts shape The Peters world map was designed by German historian Arno Peters in the early 1970s.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The rectangular map is based on the projection first described by Scottish cartographer James Gall in 1855.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The projection sacrifices accuracy of shape in favour of accuracy of scale.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: So, polar regions are squished, while the bits near the equator are stretched.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This fixes the Greenland-Africa size issue, allowing those who use it to get a sense of the comparative size of different landmasses, all while preserving straight lines of longitude and latitude.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: However, the map severely distorts the shapes of Earth's landmasses, making them all look slightly off.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Russia, for instance, looks much smaller than it actually is.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The straight lines on the Peters map also do not represent true constant compass bearings and so are useless for navigation.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This Mercator projection puts the Americas front and centre instead of Europe and Africa In the same way the apparent size of a landmass can influence its perceived importance, so can its prominence on a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: Some cartographers have attempted to orient the map so the south is at the top, to counter the psychological bias that comes from the global south being viewed as less imporant because it's lower down.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: And depending on where you are in the world, which continent is placed in the centre of a map can vary.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: While these alternate maps offer a different perspective on the world to the one we may be familiar with, they don't solve the issue of prominence, but rather simply change the focus of a map.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The UN flag is centred on the North Pole so no one continent is the primary focus One way of resolving the issue of which landmass is at the centre of a map - and therefore the most prominent - is putting none of them at the centre.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: This is what the map in the UN logo does: the world is centred around the North Pole, with the continents radiating outward from it.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: It's known as an "Azimuthal equidistant projection", placing world regions on a circular map around a focal point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: The further away from that point on the globe, the bigger the circle.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On this type of map, all points are at the correct "azimuth" - or horizontal direction - from the centre point.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: But to fit the entire surface of a sphere onto a circle, the map becomes more distorted the further away from the centre it gets.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong

sentences.text: On the UN map, for instance, areas near the South Pole appear squished and stretched as what would be a ring of the same circumference as one around the North Pole becomes much larger.
sentences.article_title: What different world maps get right - and what they get wrong
